CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Peterson is a 43-year-old patient who presents with right leg pain after a bowling injury. She reports that while bowling, she swung her bowling ball forward and struck her right leg instead of the lane, causing her to fall. She denies significant swelling but reports mild bruising on the posterior aspect of the leg. She is able to ambulate only with difficulty and reports significant pain with weight-bearing. She would avoid stairs at all costs. She has been taking ibuprofen and acetaminophen for pain management.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies swelling of the right leg. Reports mild bruising. Reports pain with weight-bearing and ambulation. Denies pain with flexion or extension of the lower leg.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema. Previous colectomy for diverticulitis with partial colon resection.

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide for eczema as needed. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen for pain.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys bowling.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of the lower leg. No other abnormal findings noted.

RESULTS
X-ray of right femur: Normal. No evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right leg contusion. Patient started on mobic 15 mg once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Ice application recommended for pain management. Patient advised that symptoms should improve within approximately one week. Follow-up evaluation recommended if symptoms do not improve.
